1	# Developer Workforce & Compensation Trends — 2024 Stack Overflow Survey
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/work
     5	
     6	## Employment Status
     7	
     8	84% of the 65,437 respondents are currently working (full-time, part-time, or freelancing). Full-time employment is the dominant mode at 69%, followed by independent contracting/freelancing at 16.4% and full-time students at 13.2%.
     9	
    10	In the United States specifically, full-time employment dropped from 69% in 2023 to 64.8% in 2024. In the U.K. and Ukraine, non-full-time respondents lean toward independent contracting, while in Germany and India they are more likely to be full-time students.
    11	
    12	## Work Environment Trends
    13	
    14	Hybrid work remains the most common arrangement at 42%, consistent with 2023. Remote work accounts for 38%. In-person work has risen for the third consecutive year — from 15% in 2022 to 16% in 2023 to 20% in 2024 — signaling a gradual return-to-office trend.
    15	
    16	## Company Size
    17	
    18	47% of respondents work for organizations with fewer than 100 employees. The distribution across 42,827 respondents:
    19	
    20	| Company Size | Share |
    21	|---|---|
    22	| Freelancer / solo | 6.1% |
    23	| 2–9 employees | 10.4% |
    24	| 10–19 employees | 8.9% |
    25	| 20–99 employees | 21.2% |
    26	| 100–499 employees | 18.5% |
    27	| 500–999 employees | 6.7% |
    28	| 1,000–4,999 employees | 11.0% |
    29	| 5,000–9,999 employees | 3.8% |
    30	| 10,000+ employees | 11.4% |
    31	
    32	## Salary by Developer Type
    33	
    34	Median annual compensation (USD, all respondents) varies dramatically by role. The top and bottom roles are shown below (22,677 salary responses, 34.7% response rate):
    35	
    36	| Developer Type | Median Salary (USD) | Avg. Years Experience |
    37	|---|---|---|
    38	| Senior Executive | $127,388 | ~17 |
    39	| Dev Advocate | $124,203 | ~16 |
    40	| Manager | $115,999 | ~15 |
    41	| Dev Experience | $109,483 | ~12 |
    42	| SRE | $99,099 | ~10 |
    43	| Cloud Infra. Engineer | $96,666 | ~13 |
    44	| Blockchain | $85,925 | ~9 |
    45	| Product Manager | $80,000 | ~14 |
    46	| Full-stack | $63,333 | ~10 |
    47	| Front-end | $48,787 | ~8 |
    48	| Student | $15,466 | ~2 |
    49	
    50	Site reliability engineers and cloud infrastructure engineers are the highest-paid purely technical roles, reflecting their critical importance in keeping digital services running. Regionally, mobile developers earn more in the U.S., data engineers top the charts in Germany and Ukraine, and back-end developers lead in India and the U.K.
    51	
    52	![Salary by developer type — bar chart](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    53	
    54	![Salary vs. experience by developer type — scatter plot](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    55	
    56	## Salary by Programming Language
    57	
    58	Developers using niche functional languages earn the most. The overall reported salary range has dropped roughly $10K compared to 2023, now averaging $60–75K USD vs. $70–85K USD last year.
    59	
    60	| Language | Median Salary (USD) | Avg. Years Experience |
    61	|---|---|---|
    62	| Erlang | ~$97,000 | ~12 |
    63	| Clojure | ~$95,000 | ~11 |
    64	| Elixir | ~$93,000 | ~11 |
    65	| Perl | ~$90,000 | ~19 |
    66	| Ruby | ~$89,000 | ~11 |
    67	| Scala | ~$88,000 | ~9 |
    68	| Go | ~$76,000 | ~9 |
    69	| Python | ~$67,000 | ~9 |
    70	| JavaScript | ~$64,000 | ~10 |
    71	| PHP | ~$49,000 | ~10 |
    72	| Dart | ~$44,000 | ~8 |
    73	| Prolog | ~$43,000 | ~9 |
    74	
    75	![Salary vs. experience by language — scatter plot](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    76	
    77	## Technology Purchasing Influence
    78	
    79	62% of respondents have influence over technology purchases at their organizations. Senior executives (99%), engineering managers (87%), and product managers (77%) wield the most influence. 60% of respondents prefer a build-and-buy approach over purely building or buying. Starting a free trial (75%) and asking other developers (73%) are the top methods for evaluating new tools.
    80	
    81	## Key Findings
    82	
    83	- **Full-time employment is softening**: U.S. full-time employment fell 4 percentage points year-over-year; freelancing and contracting remain significant at 16%+.
    84	- **In-person work is creeping back**: now at 20%, up from 15% in 2022, though hybrid (42%) still dominates.
    85	- **DevRel and leadership roles command premium pay**: Senior Executives ($127K), Dev Advocates ($124K), and Managers ($116K) top the salary chart, all with 15+ years average experience.
    86	- **Niche functional languages correlate with higher pay**: Erlang, Clojure, and Elixir developers earn >$93K median, while mainstream languages like JavaScript and PHP sit well below $65K.
    87	- **Developers are key purchase influencers**: with 62% having a say in tech buying decisions, vendor strategies should target individual contributors, not just management.

    51	
    52	# PPTX Manipulation Skill
    53	
    54	## Overview
    55	
    56	This skill enables programmatic creation, editing, and manipulation of Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations using the **python-pptx** library. Create professional slides with text, shapes, images, charts, and tables without manual editing.
    57	
    58	## How to Use
    59	
    60	1. Describe the presentation you want to create or modify
    61	2. Provide content, data, or images to include
    62	3. I'll generate python-pptx code and execute it
    63	
    64	**Example prompts:**
    65	- "Create a 10-slide pitch deck from this outline"
    66	- "Add a chart to slide 3 with this data"
    67	- "Extract all text from this presentation"
    68	- "Generate slides from this markdown content"
    69	
    70	## Domain Knowledge
    71	
    72	### python-pptx Fundamentals
    73	
    74	```python
    75	from pptx import Presentation
    76	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
    77	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
    78	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
    79	
    80	# Create new presentation
    81	prs = Presentation()
    82	
    83	# Or open existing
    84	prs = Presentation('existing.pptx')
    85	```
    86	
    87	### Presentation Structure
    88	```
    89	Presentation
    90	├── slide_layouts (predefined layouts)
    91	├── slides (individual slides)
    92	│   ├── shapes (text, images, charts)
    93	│   │   ├── text_frame (paragraphs)
    94	│   │   └── table (rows, cells)
    95	│   └── placeholders (title, content)
    96	└── slide_masters (templates)
    97	```
    98	
    99	### Slide Layouts
   100	```python
   101	# Common layout indices (may vary by template)
   102	TITLE_SLIDE = 0
   103	TITLE_CONTENT = 1
   104	SECTION_HEADER = 2
   105	TWO_CONTENT = 3
   106	COMPARISON = 4
   107	TITLE_ONLY = 5
   108	BLANK = 6
   109	
   110	# Add slide with layout
   111	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[TITLE_CONTENT]
   112	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   113	```
   114	
   115	### Adding Content
   116	
   117	#### Title Slide
   118	```python
   119	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0]  # Title slide
   120	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   121	
   122	title = slide.shapes.title
   123	subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]
   124	
   125	title.text = "Quarterly Report"
   126	subtitle.text = "Q4 2024 Performance Review"
   127	```
   128	
   129	#### Text Content
   130	```python
   131	# Using placeholder
   132	body = slide.placeholders[1]
   133	tf = body.text_frame
   134	tf.text = "First bullet point"
   135	
   136	# Add more paragraphs
   137	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   138	p.text = "Second bullet point"
   139	p.level = 0
   140	
   141	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   142	p.text = "Sub-bullet"
   143	p.level = 1
   144	```
   145	
   146	#### Text Box
   147	```python
   148	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   149	
   150	left = Inches(1)
   151	top = Inches(2)
   152	width = Inches(4)
   153	height = Inches(1)
   154	
   155	txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
   156	tf = txBox.text_frame
   157	
   158	p = tf.paragraphs[0]
   159	p.text = "Custom text box"
   160	p.font.bold = True
   161	p.font.size = Pt(18)
   162	```
   163	
   164	#### Shapes
   165	```python
   166	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
   167	
   168	# Rectangle
   169	shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
   170	    MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
   171	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # left, top
   172	    Inches(3), Inches(1.5) # width, height
   173	)
   174	shape.text = "Rectangle with text"
   175	
   176	# Common shapes:
   177	# MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   178	# MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, CHEVRON, ARROW_RIGHT
   179	# MSO_SHAPE.CALLOUT_ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   180	```
   181	
   182	#### Images
   183	```python
   184	# Add image
   185	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   186	    'image.png',
   187	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # position
   188	    width=Inches(4)        # auto height
   189	)
   190	
   191	# Or specify both dimensions
   192	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   193	    'logo.png',
   194	    Inches(8), Inches(0.5),
   195	    Inches(1.5), Inches(0.75)
   196	)
   197	```
   198	
   199	### Tables
   200	```python
   201	# Create table
   202	rows, cols = 4, 3
   203	left = Inches(1)
   204	top = Inches(2)
   205	width = Inches(8)
   206	height = Inches(2)
   207	
   208	table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table
   209	
   210	# Set column widths
   211	table.columns[0].width = Inches(2)
   212	table.columns[1].width = Inches(3)
   213	table.columns[2].width = Inches(3)
   214	
   215	# Add headers
   216	headers = ['Product', 'Q3 Sales', 'Q4 Sales']
   217	for i, header in enumerate(headers):
   218	    cell = table.cell(0, i)
   219	    cell.text = header
   220	    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   221	
   222	# Add data
   223	data = [
   224	    ['Widget A', '$10,000', '$12,500'],
   225	    ['Widget B', '$8,000', '$9,200'],
   226	    ['Widget C', '$15,000', '$18,000'],
   227	]
   228	for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data, 1):
   229	    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data):
   230	        table.cell(row_idx, col_idx).text = value
   231	```
   232	
   233	### Charts
   234	```python
   235	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   236	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   237	
   238	# Chart data
   239	chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   240	chart_data.categories = ['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4']
   241	chart_data.add_series('Sales', (19.2, 21.4, 16.7, 23.8))
   242	chart_data.add_series('Expenses', (12.1, 15.3, 14.2, 18.1))
   243	
   244	# Add chart
   245	x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(8), Inches(4)
   246	chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   247	    XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED,
   248	    x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
   249	).chart
   250	
   251	# Customize
   252	chart.has_legend = True
   253	chart.legend.include_in_layout = False
   254	```
   255	
   256	### Formatting
   257	
   258	#### Text Formatting
   259	```python
   260	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   261	
   262	run = p.runs[0]
   263	run.font.name = 'Arial'
   264	run.font.size = Pt(24)
   265	run.font.bold = True
   266	run.font.italic = True
   267	run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x66, 0xCC)
   268	```
   269	
   270	#### Shape Fill & Line
   271	```python
   272	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   273	
   274	shape.fill.solid()
   275	shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x80, 0x00)
   276	
   277	shape.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
   278	shape.line.width = Pt(2)
   279	```
   280	
   281	#### Paragraph Alignment
   282	```python
   283	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
   284	
   285	p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER  # LEFT, RIGHT, JUSTIFY
   286	```
   287	
   288	## Best Practices
   289	
   290	1. **Use Templates**: Start with a .pptx template for consistent branding
   291	2. **Layout First**: Plan slide structure before coding
   292	3. **Reuse Slide Masters**: Maintain consistency across presentations
   293	4. **Optimize Images**: Compress images before adding
   294	5. **Test Output**: Always verify generated presentations
   295	
   296	## Common Patterns
   297	
   298	### Slide Deck Generator
   299	```python
   300	def create_deck(title, slides_content):
   301	    prs = Presentation()
   302	    
   303	    # Title slide
   304	    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   305	    slide.shapes.title.text = title
   306	    
   307	    # Content slides
   308	    for slide_data in slides_content:
   309	        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   310	        slide.shapes.title.text = slide_data['title']
   311	        
   312	        body = slide.placeholders[1]
   313	        tf = body.text_frame
   314	        for i, point in enumerate(slide_data['points']):
   315	            if i == 0:
   316	                tf.text = point
   317	            else:
   318	                p = tf.add_paragraph()
   319	                p.text = point
   320	    
   321	    return prs
   322	```
   323	
   324	### Data-Driven Charts
   325	```python
   326	def add_bar_chart(slide, title, categories, values):
   327	    from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   328	    from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   329	    
   330	    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   331	    chart_data.categories = categories
   332	    chart_data.add_series('Values', values)
   333	    
   334	    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   335	        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED,
   336	        Inches(1), Inches(2),
   337	        Inches(8), Inches(4),
   338	        chart_data
   339	    ).chart
   340	    
   341	    chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = title
   342	    return chart
   343	```
   344	
   345	## Examples
   346	
   347	### Example 1: Create a Pitch Deck
   348	```python
   349	from pptx import Presentation
   350	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   351	
   352	prs = Presentation()

   359	# Slide 2: Problem

   365	p.text = "Average worker spends 20% of time on document tasks"

   368	# Slide 3: Solution
   369	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   370	slide.shapes.title.text = "Our Solution"
   371	body = slide.placeholders[1].text_frame
   372	body.text = "AI-powered document automation"
   373	body.add_paragraph().text = "90% faster processing"
   374	body.add_paragraph().text = "99.5% accuracy"
   375	body.add_paragraph().text = "Works with existing tools"
   376	
   377	# Slide 4: Market
   378	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])  # Title only
   379	slide.shapes.title.text = "Market Opportunity: $50B by 2028"
   380	
   381	# Add chart
   382	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   383	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   384	
   385	data = CategoryChartData()
   386	data.categories = ['2024', '2025', '2026', '2027', '2028']
   387	data.add_series('Market Size ($B)', [30, 35, 40, 45, 50])
   388	
   389	slide.shapes.add_chart(
   390	    XL_CHART_TYPE.LINE,
   391	    Inches(1), Inches(1.5),
   392	    Inches(8), Inches(5),
   393	    data
   394	)
   395	
   396	prs.save('pitch_deck.pptx')
   397	```
   398	
   399	### Example 2: Report with Data Table
   400	```python
   401	from pptx import Presentation
   402	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   403	
   404	prs = Presentation()
   405	
   406	# Title slide
   407	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   408	slide.shapes.title.text = "Sales Performance Report"
   409	slide.placeholders[1].text = "Q4 2024"
   410	
   411	# Data slide
   412	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])
   413	slide.shapes.title.text = "Regional Performance"
   414	
   415	# Create table
   416	table = slide.shapes.add_table(5, 4, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(9), Inches(4)).table
   417	
   418	# Headers
   419	headers = ['Region', 'Revenue', 'Growth', 'Target']
   420	for i, h in enumerate(headers):
   421	    table.cell(0, i).text = h
   422	    table.cell(0, i).text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   423	
   424	# Data

def add_background_shape(slide, color=LIGHT_GRAY):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
        0, 0, prs.slide_width, prs.slide_height
    )
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    # Send to back
    spTree = slide.shapes._spTree
    sp = shape._element
    spTree.remove(sp)
    spTree.insert(2, sp)

def add_header_bar(slide, title_text, subtitle_text=None):
    # Dark blue header bar
    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
        0, 0, prs.slide_width, Inches(1.2)
    )
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BLUE
    bar.line.fill.background()
    
    # Title
    title_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(0.25), Inches(12), Inches(0.7))
    tf = title_box.text_frame
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = title_text
    p.font.size = Pt(28)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = WHITE
    p.font.name = "Calibri"

        p2.text = subtitle_text
        p2.font.size = Pt(14)
        p2.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xCC, 0xCC, 0xCC)
